quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You miss your turn or exit on a freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your current lane.
Keep driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder or freeway is illegal.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even when no other cars are visible.
Signal only if there is traffic nearby.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even when no other cars are visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from the curb. Make this a habit so you don't skip signaling.

questions.question: Taking drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Makes alcohol's effects weaker on your driving.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter) can harm your brain and make driving unsafe. Mixing alcohol with other drugs greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, remember:

options.text: Roads are very slippery right when rain starts.
You need extra space to stop.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are dangerously slippery, especially right after rain starts. Your tires sit on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down when there is heavy rain, standing water, or slush to keep your tires from losing grip.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a sharp right turn coming up.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and get ready to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic.
May go through if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: May go through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if it is clear. You may also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, let other vehicles and pedestrians go first.

questions.question: A stop sign is shaped like a(n):
questions.explanation: Only stop signs are octagonal. All eight-sided signs tell drivers to come to a complete stop before going.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Everyone in the car every time it is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car every time it is driven.
questions.explanation: Make sure everyone in your car wears a seat belt. In a crash, an unbelted person becomes a flying object and can hurt others in the vehicle.

questions.question: The driver ahead is using one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Stay farther away from that vehicle.
Know that this driver is not paying full attention.
Not copy this bad driving habit.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by looking at passengers, searching in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming while driving. If another driver looks distracted, keep extra distance from them because they are more likely to crash.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is one who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while having a conversation while driving.
Only watches the car directly ahead.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by looking at passengers, searching in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming while driving. Keep scanning the road, checking mirrors, and watching your gauges often. These safe habits will help you stay focused while driving.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing down over a lane means you can use that lane.

questions.question: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Pull to the right side of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle using lights or a siren. If you are in an intersection, go through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce off fog and make it harder to see. Use fog lights if your vehicle has them.

questions.question: A driver with a probationary license must practice driving for up to:
questions.explanation: With a probationary license, you must drive alone for at least one year before getting your regular driver license. Follow all rules for probationary license holders during this time.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop right away. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop bleeding but do not move injured people. Wait for help to arrive.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you are doing.

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are only found in construction zones.
Are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers position their vehicles, show safe passing zones, and warn about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Passing poor drivers to get ahead of them in traffic.
Staying very close to the vehicle in front of you.
Quickly changing lanes and moving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations and act before a crash happens. It helps you avoid accidents with aggressive, reckless, or impaired drivers.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: You are entering a reduced speed zone.
You are leaving a reduced speed zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are leaving a reduced speed zone.
questions.explanation: The "End school zone" sign marks where the lower school zone speed limit ends. You can resume normal speed after this sign.

questions.question: You should not pass:

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Never pass if you cannot see ahead clearly, if there is oncoming traffic, at an intersection, before or on a railroad crossing or bridge, or in any no passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road with a median or center turn lane.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition with proper tread depth.
Keep your tires inflated to the correct pressure.
Slow down when driving in the rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with proper tread depth and correct air pressure. Slow down when driving in the rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes:

options.text: Look into the left side mirror.
Look into the right side mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: The "No zone" is:

options.text: A term used to describe blind spots around a truck or bus.
A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.
The television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A term used to describe blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on each side, in the rear, and in the front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when turning. This allows you to control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to unexpected situations.

questions.question: Alcohol:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows brain activity and reduces the skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, what must you do?

options.text: You can either continue through or exit the freeway.
You can stay in your lane and continue through.
You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means that lane leads off the freeway and does not continue through. If you stay in that lane, you must exit. You can change lanes to continue through the freeway.

questions.question: Which of these can impair your driving and result in a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many things can impair driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription and over-the-counter medicines.

questions.question: When do you NOT have to stop for an ice cream truck?

options.text: When it shows flashing red lights
When it shows a stop signal arm
When a person is crossing to or from the truck
When driving on a dual highway on the opposite side of a median or safety island

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving on a dual highway on the opposite side of a median or safety island
questions.explanation: You must stop for an ice cream truck with flashing red lights unless you are on a dual highway on the opposite side of a safety island or median. Then you can continue past slowly at no more than 15 mph.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: The driver and all passengers must wear a seat belt. Not wearing one is a violation. The driver is responsible for making sure passengers under 18 wear a seat belt.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a drunk driver?
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include weaving, driving too slow, speeding, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights flash or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not go around the gate.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles

questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the rear that cannot be seen in mirrors.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you only have a few drinks

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or taking drugs. It is dangerous to you and to others on the road.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they:

options.text: Will drive the same as usual
Can drive faster because they are more alert
Should calm down and focus before driving
Should call a friend to talk while driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Should calm down and focus before driving
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness make it hard to drive well. Your mind is on something else instead of the road. Take time to calm down and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign means a steep hill is coming. Be ready to adjust your speed.

questions.question: What are the most effective safety restraints in a traffic crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash. They also more than double your chance of avoiding serious injury. Airbags work best when used with safety belts. They provide extra protection in front-end crashes. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination could multiply the effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination could multiply the effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs increases how much each one affects you. For example, one drink plus a cold medicine could affect you as much as several drinks without any medicine.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to check if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to make sure no one is in your blind spot.

questions.question: What is a good way to help relieve fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, stop for a short break every two hours. If you become drowsy, pull off the road to a safe place and take a nap or stay overnight.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle defect that may affect safe operation. What should you do?

options.text: Correct the defect as soon as possible.
Correct the defect when you can afford it.
Drive the vehicle at slower speeds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Correct the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that may affect safe vehicle operation right away. Do not drive the vehicle until the defect is fixed.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. What should you do?

options.text: Not worry about it because all vehicles are the same.
Hide from your friend that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn how to operate all the vehicle's equipment before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn how to operate all the vehicle's equipment before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend a few minutes learning where and how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any defects before driving.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: No less safe than driving under other conditions.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely risky. It endangers you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers. Keeping your attention on the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that mirrors cannot show. Check them by turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, the driver must show:
questions.explanation: When stopped, you must show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You are required to have all three documents in your vehicle when driving.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road without bicycle lanes and see a bicyclist ahead traveling the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming, then pass while leaving plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. The bicyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to let the bicyclist know you are about to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming, then pass while leaving plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like you would any other vehicle, but carefully. Leave at least 3 feet of space on regular roads or 5 feet on higher speed roads or when passing multiple bicyclists. Do not honk loudly as it may startle the rider and cause a crash.
